title: What do we notice about the populations of Indian cities?
description: A table gives the populations of twenty Indian cities in two thousand eleven and two thousand one. The board compares the two columns row by row, finds the one city that fell, and builds a title. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking every city grew.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the two columns row by row before writing an observation, and name the table by what it shows and when. Ask the class what they notice in the first three rows before the whole table is read. Watch for students who write that every city grew without checking each row.

source: Write a general observation about the table and an appropriate title
video_script.why: The child can read lakh and crore numbers and compare them, and now reads a whole table of them to say what it shows.
video_script.substitution: Compare the two columns row by row, note the usual pattern and the exception, then name the table by what it shows and when.
video_script.anchor: A table of Indian cities with two columns, the population in 2011 and the population in 2001.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that most rows have a bigger number in 2011 and says every city grew. In the Kolkata row 44,86,679 is smaller than 45,72,876, so one city fell.
video_script.payoff_line: Most cities grew, but Kolkata fell

final_answer.value: Most cities grew from 2001 to 2011 (Kolkata fell). Title: Population of some Indian cities in 2001 and 2011
final_answer.spoken: most cities grew from two thousand one to two thousand eleven, but Kolkata fell, and a good title is Population of some Indian cities in two thousand one and two thousand eleven

hold_back: Population of some Indian cities in 2001 and 2011
never_show: the full title before the answer beat
maths_rules: Mumbai: 1,24,42,373 is more than 1,19,78,450; Bengaluru: 84,25,970 is more than 43,01,326; Chennai: 46,81,087 is more than 43,43,645
in nearly every row the 2011 number is larger, so most cities grew
Kolkata: 44,86,679 is less than 45,72,876; 45,72,876 − 44,86,679 = 86,197, so Kolkata fell by about 86,000
a title says what the table shows, which cities and which years: Population of some Indian cities in 2001 and 2011
video_script.design: One idea: compare each row, note the pattern and the exception, then title the table. Wrong idea: Keeko says every city grew. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
